To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
tractable generalizable reinforcement learning is possible if and only if the environments are similar.

(1) Weak Proximity, which requires environments to have highly-similar transition and reward functions, is a necessary condition for efficient generalization; (2) Strong Proximity, which additionally requires the environments to share a policy providing near-optimal value, is a sufficient condition for efficient generalizaiton; and (3) the two conditions are incomparable in the sense that neither is implied by the other.

tractable generalizable RL is impossible in the absence of Strong Proximity, but is possible with Strong Proximity, even in the worst case, even with a generative model, and even when individual environments are efficiently solvable.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question: when is tractable generalization possible in RL? We answer this question by providing both a negative result (tractable generalization is not possible under weak proximity) and a positive result (tractable representation learning is possible under strong proximity).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
generalizable RL is tractable only in the presence of Strong Proximity.
tractable generalizable RL is possible when the environments satisfy Strong Proximity, and impossible in the absence of Weak Proximity.
tractable generalizable RL is possible when the environments share a policy providing the optimal value function, but in the absence of such structure, generalizable RL is not tractable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tractable generalizable RL is impossible in the general case, but possible under certain structural conditions.
tractable generalizable RL is possible when environments are similar in a strong sense.
tractable generalizable reinforcement learning requires environments to be similar, but similar in a very specific way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tractable generalizable RL requires environments to share more structure than just similar reward functions and transition dynamics.
generalizable RL agents are only tractable when the environments share enough structure.
tractable generalizable reinforcement learning is impossible in the most general sense.
